evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md (259 words, 5 prose paragraphs) is a first-person request from a small firm: line 1 'Kittle & Rowe is a small law firm, and our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last. We want a secure chat where each client talks to us inside their legal matter...'; line 3 states priorities in the client's own terms ('Two things matter more than anything else. First, ethical walls... Second, retention...'); line 9 asks them to 'try it the way we'll use it, in a browser'. Against the quality-checks.md:11 defect list: a grep for numbered items, bullets and shall/MUST finds none (the only 'must' hits are in narrative sentences on line 3); there is no spec table, feature matrix, framework choice, file layout beyond the template-mandated deliverable paths (/app/server.js, /app/app.db, /assets/seed_data.json on line 5), and no endpoint list. The detail lives in the three notes, which are also written as narrative explanation ('Our clients ask several things at once, so answers have to stay with their question'); the only table is the account roster in walls-and-retention.md, which is seed/credential data the profile expects, not a feature matrix. The Node 22/Express/better-sqlite3/port 3000/GET /api/health facts in integration.md are the template runtime contract (row 4's territory), framed as 'How we run it', not a task-added build recipe, and are absent from instruction.md itself. Counterexample search: this row grades prompt prose, so no broken-app or conforming-alternative outcome is affected by it; I found no wording that would make a reader treat the prompt as a checklist. No runtime evidence is required for this row; the raw-evidence index was not needed.
